Four RTX PRO 6000 cards on PCIe 4 with no NVLink, training a 500M-total/~330M-active MoE at an effective global batch of ~1M tokens — the same regime — measured "gradient communication accounted for 50% of the single-step time"; enabling `no_sync()` so the all-reduce fires only on the tenth micro-step cut wall-clock from under 18 hours to 13.2 hours, leaving ~1.7% in sync [[a-13-hour-training-experiment-on-a-pc-workstation-why-optimization-begins-with-m]] (T2).

The 2× only reproduces if you force fp32 gradient reduction via `MixedPrecision(reduce_dtype=torch.float32)`; FSDP's default `reduce_dtype=None` "still running gradient reduction in low precision" [[fullyshardeddataparallel-pytorch-213-documentation]] (T3).

What remains is the bubble: (5−1)/32 = 12.5% for 1F1B at 32 micro-batches, ~4.2% for zero-bubble schedules, and under 4.5% measured for RoundPipe with asynchronous optimizer updates [[efficient-training-on-multiple-consumer-gpus-with]] (T2/T3).

It shards optimizer state and gradients but not parameters, so it costs 4.8 B/param × 7B = 33.6 GB of model state (T4) and its communication is "exactly 2Ψ" — the same byte volume as DDP's all-reduce [[zero-memory-optimizations-toward-training-trillion-parameter-models-sc20]] (T3) — while preserving Adam, so comparability with the control survives.

On the closest published fabric analogue — ten RTX 3090s sharing ~3 GB/s of PCIe with P2P disabled — ZeRO-2 beats DDP at every GPU count, by +27% at four and +50% at eight [[pcie-110-gpu-스케일링]] (T2); on 8×A100 with NVSwitch it loses 2.90×, because the ~2.4 s delta was CPU-side Python execution of per-parameter hooks [[perf-29-throughput-by-switching-from-deepspeed-to-ddp-issue-177-tensorautoopen-2]] (T2).

It is measured on this fabric class — on four RTX A6000s over PCIe with no NVLink, bf16 gradients moved plain DDP from 2.06× to 2.65× at 124M and 1.91× to 2.72× at 355M [[ddp-on-a-pcie-only-4x-rtx-a6000-no-nvlink-plain-ddp-gave-2x-bf16-gradient-compre]] (T2) — but at the corrected window it is worth only ~3% of step time: halving a 4.0 GB payload saves 1.85 s against 56.3 s of compute, and the ~18% it buys belongs to the plan's own 36% premise.

The cluster's consensus runs against intuition — compression pays more, not less, on slow fabrics: AGoQ's 8-bit all-reduce is 3.7× at 10 Gbps against 3.4× at 200 Gbps [[agoq-activation-and-gradient-quantization-for]], and CERAR cuts Pythia-1.4B by 17.3% on PCIe while running 33% slower on NVLink [[communication-efficient-distributed-training]] (T3).

PaLM states it explicitly: "an N-parameter decoder-only model requires 6N matmul FLOPs per token seen (2N for forward and 4N for backward)" and separately that "The matmuls in dense self-attention add 6LH(2QT) FLOPs per token", so the theoretical peak is R = P(6N + 12LHQT) [[palm-scaling-language-modeling-with-pathways]] (T3).

Megatron-Core corroborates from measurement: "at 64K tokens, SDPA consumes 69% of FLOPs, compared to only 10–15% in short-sequence scenarios" [[scalable-training-of-mixture-of-experts-models-with]] (T3).

It sits within a factor of four of the adjacent-hardware measurement at the same batch regime, 1.7% amortized after `no_sync()` [[a-13-hour-training-experiment-on-a-pc-workstation-why-optimization-begins-with-m]] (T2).

SLMTrainBench measures a 505.5M model at 4k = 26,297 tok/s (39.88% MFU) and at 32k = 11,990 tok/s (63.88% MFU) on an A100 80GB PCIe, computing MFU with the same 6N + 12LHS formula: a measured per-token cost ratio of 2.19×, with a 1.60× MFU uplift absorbing 40% of the quadratic penalty [[readmemd-faircslmtrainbench-at-main]] (T3).
The pattern is systematic — 2.19–2.27× across 150M–500M — and SkyLadder's 1B model cross-checks it with a 2.20× FLOPs ratio from 8K to 32K [[skyladder-better-and-faster-pretraining-via]] (T3).

The one prototype that does work on PCIe without P2P, ThunderEP, reaches 2.00× dispatch and 1.53× combine over NCCL on 6×4090 and 6×5090 systems — but it is integrated into vLLM and evaluated on inference, with no gradient collectives [[efficient-expert-parallel-communication]] (T3).

So the corpus holds no evidence of a training-grade EP implementation for a no-P2P, no-NVLink, no-RDMA fabric — the closest are VarioPath, a PCIe-native all-to-all scheduler evaluated on inference [[variopath-workload-aware-all-to-all-communication-for-pcie-gpu-clusters]], and ThunderEP, a no-P2P dispatch/combine with no backward.

TP has no equivalent hiding place at this scale — though model-parallel communication can be overlapped with compute given an overlap-friendly schedule [[on-optimizing-the-communication-of-model-parallelism]] (T3), and on PCIe TP overtakes DP above ~20B parameters by avoiding full-parameter synchronisation [[efficient-training-on-multiple-consumer-gpus-with]] (T2).

Adafactor keeps only the per-row and per-column sums of Adam's second moment, giving state proportional to n + m rather than nm [[adafactor-adaptive-learning-rates-with-sublinear-memory-cost]] (T3), and 8-bit Adam's block-wise quantization matches 32-bit performance at 1.5B [[published-as-a-conference-paper-at-iclr-2022]] (T3).

The indexer's score tensor is a `[B, S, H_I, T]` FP32 intermediate materialized before the head-sum, which at S=32,768 with V4-Flash dimensions is 64 GiB, with a measured peak of 129.00 GB and 317 ms on a 140 GB H200 [[streamindex-memory-bounded-compressed-sparse]] (T3); the pure-PyTorch cuDNN reference has the same defect, materializing `(B, S_q, H_q, S_k)` FP32 at 68.7 GB for 32k/H_q=16 [[dsa_referencepy]] (T3/T4).

The tuned stacks are built on Hopper's `wgmma.mma_async`; Ampere has only `mma.sync`, and TileLang's own fallback to it "runs 1.81× slower", so an sm_80 build is possible-but-slow rather than impossible [[tilelangexamplesdeepseek_v32-at-main-tile-aitilelang-github]] (T2).

The one arch-portable Triton stack is worse than slow: StreamIndex's attention forward reaches only 8% of H200 BF16 peak at V4-Pro dimensions against TileLang's 40% on the same shape [[streamindex-memory-bounded-compressed-sparse]] (T3), and at 8% of peak even a 64× FLOP reduction does not produce a usable training kernel.

The indexer, not the sparse MLA, is the hard half — HISA measures 1.6 ms for the Sparse MLA operator against 5.6 ms for the indexer at 64K on A100, and concludes "the main performance bottleneck in DSA lies in the indexer rather than in Sparse MLA itself" [[published-as-a-conference-paper-at-colm-2026]] (T3).

The layer mix bounds how much of that matters: V4.1-Flash ships 2 SWA + 4 Full + 4 Reindex + 30 Reuse over 40 layers, so 32 of 40 run no indexer and the 16,384-candidate cap binds on only the 4 decoder Reindex layers [[deepseek-v41-flash]] (T3).

Its current release states its scope verbatim: Its current release lists its supported scope as sm_100a / sm_103a and Ascend 950, DeepSeek-V4.1 only, and it has dropped Hopper entirely [[github-deepseek-aiflashmla-flashmla-efficient-multi-head-latent-attention-kernel]] (T2).

The production sparse-attention forward for CSA2 does not run on Hopper, let alone Ampere. flash-attention's sparse-MLA forward and backward kernels are SM100-only files (`flash_fwd_mla_sm100.py`, `flash_bwd_mla_sm100.py`) [[cutebwdsm100-add-sparse-mla-deepseek-v4-backward-kernels-2621-dao-ailabflash-att]] (T2), and the Ampere port of FlashMLA exposes only paged-KV decode, has no backward, and reports that "the performance of Ampere is currently poor due to register overflow" — 464 GB/s and 59 TFLOPS on A100 SXM against 2,039 GB/s and 312 TFLOPS peak [[github-pzhao-engflashmla-github]] (T2).

The only sm_80 path is vLLM's `TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`, which adds a Triton-based sparse MLA attention backend (`TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`) "so DSA sparse-MLA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) can run on GPUs where DeepGEMM and FlashMLA-Sparse are unavailable" [[attention-triton_mla_sparse-backend-for-sm80sm121-sparse-mla-rebase-takeover-of]] (T2).

It reports up to 1.25× and 1.09× on average end-to-end training speedup over the Triton NSA kernel, and up to 2.47× and 1.86× on average over full attention [[published-as-a-conference-paper-at-iclr-2026]] (T3).

The fla-org Triton implementation reproduces a shrinking advantage: 2.66× forward at 16,384 tokens, 1.35× at 8,192, and 0.72× at 4,096 — NSA is slower than flash at short context [[github-fla-orgnative-sparse-attention-efficient-triton-implementations-for-nativ]] (T2).

FSA reports directly that vanilla NSA lags behind full attention in many tested cases, even with its sparse attention mechanism: when the sequence length is 32K and one GQA group contains one query head, NSA consistently falls short of full attention [[published-as-a-conference-paper-at-iclr-2026]] (T3).

Top-k is non-differentiable, so the indexer is trained by a clipped-log KL distillation against the main attention distribution rather than end-to-end [[dsa_referencepy]] (T3), which adds a second score-tensor forward and backward and a separate loss term to every step; and the indexer's cost is additive and measured at 3.5× the kernel it feeds.

FSA's official implementation is "well tested with NVIDIA Ampere or Hopper GPUs (e.g., A100 SXM, H20, H100 PCIe, H100 NVL, H100 SXM, H200 SXM)", supports "Training and inference (prefill)", and calls `loss.backward()` through a 65,536 + 32,768-token batch; it requires `flash-attn==2.6.3` [[github-relaxed-system-labflash-sparse-attention-efficient-implementations-of-nat]] (T2).
The fla-org Triton NSA ships full training support via `flame` [[github-fla-orgnative-sparse-attention-efficient-triton-implementations-for-nativ]] (T2).

MoBA is the fallback, also pinned to `flash-attn==2.6.3` [[github-moonshotaimoba-moba-mixture-of-block-attention-for-long-context-llms-gith]] (T2), but it is compute-neutral at 32k and lossy alone: trailing LM loss at 32K is 1.546 against 1.464 for full attention [[moba-mixture-of-block-attention-for]] (T3).
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash trains sparse attention from scratch at 64K across 45T tokens [[deepseek-v41-flash]] (T3) — a capability receipt, not a speedup receipt, and at 64K rather than 32k.

**Every sparse-attention 32k win is an adaptation-stage result.** One side holds that sparse attention delivers large measured 32k wins: NSA reports 6.3× forward and 3.4× backward at 32k on A100 with a quality win, and LongCat's LSA claims parity with full attention and native training to 1M tokens [[native-sparse-attention-hardware-aligned-and-natively]], [[longcat-sparse-attention-taming-the-lightning-via]] (T3/T2).

**P2P has two incompatible data-movement figures and the larger one is unverified.** One side holds that BAR1 P2P works and moves data at 1.68 GB/s each way at Gen2 x4 on 12/12 pairs [[github-bayleycmpunlocker-a-cmpunlocker-fork-with-working-p2p-on-sys-4028gr-trt2]] (T2).

The decisive fact is the one nobody cites: on a four-card PLX rig at Gen2 x16, host-staged copy already moves large buffers at 6.21–6.30 GB/s, so P2P is 8% slower above 16 MiB and costs 25–44% on TP4 decode [[2026-10-01-cmp170hx-4card-bar1-p2p-plx-cudaipynb]] (T2).
